faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.q1: How does CloneLink download GitHub subfolders without cloning?
faq.a1: CloneLink queries the public GitHub REST API to retrieve the repository file tree for that specific subpath. It fetches the raw file contents asynchronously and packages them into a clean .zip file right inside your browser memory using JSZip.
faq.q2: Are my private repositories or GitHub tokens exposed?
faq.a2: No. CloneLink is a static, 100% client-side web application hosted on GitHub Pages. No backend server exists. Any GitHub token you optionally provide is stored exclusively in your browser's localStorage and only transmitted directly to api.github.com.
faq.q3: What GitHub URL formats are supported?
faq.a3: CloneLink supports standard HTTPS URLs (https://github.com/user/repo), SSH URLs (git@github.com:user/repo.git), shorthand (user/repo), single organization names (which expand to user/user.github.io), and deep links (https://github.com/user/repo/tree/branch/subfolder).
faq.q4: What is the difference between shallow clone and sparse-checkout?
faq.a4: A shallow clone (--depth 1) fetches only the latest commit history of the whole repository. A sparse-checkout configures Git to only populate specific directories on your local disk from the remote repository.
faq.q5: What should I do if I hit the GitHub API rate limit?
faq.a5: GitHub limits unauthenticated IP requests to 60 per hour. You can create a free Personal Access Token (classic with public_repo read permission, or fine-grained token) and paste it into the optional token field to increase your limit to 5,000 requests per hour.
